description.text: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company and its subsidiaries (the "Company" or "ADM") unlocks the power of nature to enrich the quality of life. The Company is an essential global agricultural supply chain manager and processor, providing food security by connecting local needs with global capabilities. ADM is also a premier human and animal nutrition provider, as well as a leader in health and well-being products. The Company partners with thousands of farmers around the world to purchase their crops and uses its integrated global origination, logistics, and manufacturing network to transform many of those raw commodities into an expansive array of products serving the food, feed, fuel, and industrial and consumer products sectors. The Company offers a broad portfolio of food and beverage products, from staple foods to innovative alternatives, such as natural colors and flavors, plant-based proteins, and lower-sugar, fat, and salt solutions. ADM provides human and animal nutrition ingredients and solutions that support health, productivity, and sustainability. It offers a wide range of health and well-being products, such as probiotics, enzymes, and supplements to meet the needs of consumers looking for new ways to live healthier lives. ADM is a key producer of biofuels, converting agricultural feedstocks into renewable fuels used in transportation and industrial applications.

about.description_short: ADM unlocks the power of nature to enrich the quality of life. We're an essential global agricultural supply chain manager and processor, providing food security by connecting local needs with global capabilities. We're a premier human and animal nutrition provider, offering one of the industry's broadest portfolios of ingredients and solutions from nature. We're a trailblazer in health and well-being, with an industry-leading range of products for consumers looking for new ways to live healthier lives. We're a cutting-edge innovator, guiding the way to a future of new bio-based consumer and industrial solutions. And we're leading in business-driven sustainability efforts that support a strong agricultural sector, resilient supply chains, and a vast and growing bioeconomy. Around the globe, our expertise and innovation are meeting critical needs from harvest to home.

analysis_md:
# ADM — Archer-Daniels-Midland Co
v5 run, 2026-10-14 (supersedes the v4 analysis of 2026-10-13; same moat, probabilities and growth recalibration, re-derived on v5 filing-direct data). Price $83.20 (nasdaq_quote_api); engine market cap $40,268,800,000 — just over the $40B scope line at today's price, so `in_scope_under_40b` is false (the stock is up ~44.7% YTD per Finnhub, via search).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, ttm.py output, or cited search results — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Global agricultural merchandiser and processor: Ag Services & Oilseeds (origination, storage/transport, crushing, refining), Carbohydrate Solutions (starches & sweeteners, ethanol via Vantage Corn Processors), and Nutrition (human and animal). FY2025 reported totals (earnings release, via search): revenue $80,269M, net earnings attributable to ADM $1,078M, GAAP EPS $2.23, adjusted EPS $3.43. A low-margin commodity toll-taker: FY2025 gross profit was $5,033M on that $80,269M of revenue.

Latest earnings: Q2 2026 (reported 2026-08-04) — revenue $22,681M (+7.2% YoY), GAAP EPS $1.87, adjusted EPS $1.84 (+98% YoY), total segment operating profit up 75% YoY; FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.15–5.60 from $4.15–4.70 (search results). The driver is explicit in ADM's own release: the EPA finalized 2026/2027 renewable volume obligations in March 2026, lifting crush and ethanol margins, helped by elevated energy prices. That is a policy-and-cycle rebound off a trough — real, but not a durable growth rate. Adjusted ROIC on the trailing four quarters was only 7.8% per ADM's Q2 release (via search).

Red flags: (1) the 2024 Nutrition intersegment-accounting scandal — sales between Nutrition and the other segments were not recorded at market rates, inflating Nutrition's segment profit; ADM restated segment reporting in November 2024 and settled the SEC investigation in January 2026 for $40M (prior v4 analysis of this folder; segment-only, no impact on consolidated earnings or cash flows, so the consolidated owner's-earnings history used here stands). (2) Earnings are hostage to US biofuel policy, crush margins, crop prices and trade flows — all outside management's control. (3) Owner's earnings are extremely lumpy from working-capital / readily-marketable-inventory swings (see flags).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $5,452,000,000; capex $1,248,000,000; SBC $83,000,000 (always a real cost, and small here).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $4,121,000,000 = $8.51/share** (latest FY OE/share, dcf_numbers.json)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $1,799,000,000 — far below the conservative figure. The gap is the story: FY2025 OCF was flattered by a working-capital release as revenues fell, while net income was depressed by non-cash charges (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below). Neither definition supports treating $8.51/share as run-rate.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (engine), but the conservative OE totals swing hard year to year (financials_history.csv): $5,265,000,000 (2021), $2,012,000,000 (2022), $2,854,000,000 (2023), $1,153,000,000 (2024), $4,121,000,000 (2025). This is a cyclical, working-capital-dominated cash stream, not a compounder.
- Net debt $6,597,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json), 2.59x normalized OE (diagnostics) — manageable for a commodity merchant with liquid inventories, but it is not a net-cash cushion and it does not rescue the valuation.

**TTM check (ttm.py, filing-direct, run for STALE_FY — quoted in full, not used as the base):**
- OCF: FY $5,452,000,000 − prior YTD $3,956,000,000 + current YTD $1,299,000,000 = **TTM $2,795,000,000**
- Capex: FY $1,248,000,000 − prior YTD $596,000,000 + current YTD $466,000,000 = **TTM $1,118,000,000**
- SBC: FY $83,000,000 − prior YTD $72,000,000 + current YTD $138,000,000 = **TTM $149,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **485,000,000**
- **TTM OE total $1,528,000,000 → TTM OE/share $3.15**

**Base used = normalized 3-yr median OE/share $5.27** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). Reason: both single-point alternatives are working-capital artifacts in opposite directions — the latest FY ($8.51) is inflated by a WC release in a down-revenue year, and the TTM ($3.15) is depressed by an H1 2026 WC build (H1 OCF $1,299,000,000 vs $3,956,000,000 in H1 2025) that coincided with *rising* earnings (Q2 adjusted EPS +98% YoY; guidance raised). For a commodity merchandiser whose inventories swing by billions seasonally, the median is the only one of the three bases that is not a WC-timing snapshot. The spread between the three defensible bases ($3.15 / $5.27 / $8.51) is itself the headline uncertainty — see Thoughts.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-moderate; scale without pricing power
Justification: ADM's origination, storage, transportation and processing network is genuinely hard to replicate and has survived a century of cycles, but it earns commodity returns: crush and ethanol margins are set by markets and by US biofuel policy, not by ADM, and through-cycle returns on capital are high-single-digit at best (7.8% adjusted ROIC on the trailing four quarters, at a cyclical *upswing* print). That is scale, not a wide moat.
- FOR: global origination / grain-elevator / rail-barge / export-terminal network at a scale rivals cannot quickly replicate, with real logistics optionality when trade flows shift; diversified processing footprint across oilseeds, corn and Nutrition, so no single spread carries the company; equity earnings from unconsolidated affiliates ($648M in FY2025, earnings release) including the Wilmar relationship; balance-sheet staying power through cycles (378 consecutive quarters of dividends, per the Q2 2026 call via search).
- AGAINST: commodity price-taker on both sides — ADM prices neither what it buys (corn, soy) nor most of what it sells; crush and ethanol margins are market-set, and the entire 2026 earnings recovery is explicitly policy-driven (EPA renewable volume obligations), i.e. the tailwind is a regulation, not an advantage; equally scaled, undifferentiated rivals (Bunge, Cargill, COFCO); Nutrition — the one segment that could have earned a moat premium — is where the intersegment-accounting fraud lived, and it is too small to move consolidated returns; working-capital-heavy model absorbs cash exactly when commodity prices rise; thin structural margins (FY2025 gross profit $5,033M on $80,269M revenue).
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
Growth recalibration (written reason): the engine's g_base is +4.46%, but both of its components are compromised — the revenue blend uses the corrupted revenue series (BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT below: rev CAGR 5y −17.26% and 3y −3.31% are tag artifacts; OE/share CAGR 2y +27.14% is a WC artifact) and the +4.91pp share-count adjustment is stale (BUYBACK_TAILWIND below: the count has been flat at 484–485M recently). Scenario starts were therefore set by offsets (−0.0946/−0.0446/−0.0146/+0.0154/+0.0554 vs g_base) to −5.0% / 0.0% / **+3.0%** / +6.0% / +10.0%. Probabilities skewed bearish vs defaults (15/30/30/17/8): OE volatility plus a share price that has already capitalized the RVO rebound argue for more left-tail weight. OE multipliers default 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $83.20.

Sanity check vs actual prints: scenario starts are *cash OE/share* growth, not EPS. Real revenue growth is low-single-digit (Q2 2026 revenue +7.2% YoY, FY2025 −6.15%); the guided FY2026 adjusted-EPS rebound (+50–63% vs FY2025 adjusted $3.43) is a trough/policy margin recovery on a fixed asset base, not a sustainable OE growth rate — and TTM cash OE/share actually fell to $3.15 on the H1 working-capital build. So even the super-bull start (+10.0%) sits far below the 2026 EPS print, deliberately: revenue — the thing that can compound — is growing at 2–7%, and margins mean-revert.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -5.0% | 0.75 | Biofuel policy or crush margins reverse; WC build eats cash | $24.19 | 5.92% |
| Bear | 30% | 0.0% | 0.90 | Earnings recovery proves cyclical-peak; OE stays at depressed cash levels | $35.28 | 7.72% |
| Base | 30% | 3.0% | 1.00 | Normalized median OE, modest per-share growth, margins stay thin | $44.01 | 9.13% |
| Bull | 17% | 6.0% | 1.10 | RVO-driven crush/ethanol strength persists; buybacks resume | $54.30 | 10.75% |
| Super bull | 8% | 10.0% | 1.25 | Sustained policy tailwind plus a WC-release year like FY2025 | $71.79 | 13.37% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $42.39 (−49.1% vs price), IV@12% $55.84, IV@10% $70.80, weighted IRR 8.89%, base-case IRR 9.13%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 6.33%, terminal value 17.91% of IV@15% (low — the verdict is not a terminal-value artifact), scenario spread 2.97x, net debt 2.59x normalized OE, 9.43 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.43 months ago): ttm.py was run and its full inputs are quoted above. The TTM base was *not* adopted — see BASE_DIVERGENCE; the median base is used, with the TTM figure disclosed as the bear-side evidence. The Q2 2026 earnings recovery is reflected in the scenario growth starts and in rejecting any claim that FY2025's trough earnings are the run rate.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $8.51 vs 3-yr median $5.27): both single-point bases are distorted — the latest FY by a working-capital release (maintenance OE is only $1,799,000,000 vs conservative $4,121,000,000), the TTM ($3.15) by an H1 2026 WC build during an earnings upswing. The median is the least-distorted base; resolved by using it and by weighting bear outcomes at 45% combined.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in the engine series): an EDGAR tagging break, not a divestiture. The engine's revenue tag (RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax) matches ADM's reported total revenue through 2021 ($85,249M) and then drops to $27,606,000,000 in 2022, while ADM's reported total revenue was $101,556M in 2022, $93,935M in 2023, $85,530M in 2024 and $80,269M in 2025 (earnings release / Barchart, via search). So the engine's revenue CAGRs (−17.26% 5y, −3.31% 3y, +2.39% latest YoY) are not total-revenue growth and were not trusted as such; the real top-line trend is a mid-single-digit decline from the 2022 commodity-price peak. The OE series is unaffected — it is built from OCF/capex/SBC tags, which show no such break. The genuine basis item — the November 2024 Nutrition restatement — was segment-only with no consolidated impact, so it does not break the consolidated OE history either.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025: net income $1,078,000,000 vs OCF $5,452,000,000): working capital and non-cash charges, identified in the FY2025 release (via search): $473M of asset impairment, exit and restructuring costs depressing net income, plus non-cash D&A of $1,181,000,000 (financials_history.csv), while OCF was boosted by drawing down inventories/receivables into falling revenue — the mirror image of H1 2026. Neither the NI-based maintenance OE nor the OCF-based conservative OE is a clean single-year run rate for ADM; this is the core reason the base is a 3-yr median.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real and structural — crush/ethanol spread cyclicality plus inventory-driven OCF (conservative OE totals from $1,153,000,000 to $5,265,000,000 across the last 5 years). Handled by the normalized median base, wider bear/super-bear weight (45% combined), and a super-bear OE multiplier of 0.75.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count −4.91%/yr, credited +4.91pp in the blend): stale. Diluted shares fell from 566,000,000 (2021) to 484,000,000 (2025), but the count has stopped shrinking — 493,000,000 in FY2024, 484,000,000 in FY2025, and 485,000,000 on the TTM current-YTD basis (ttm.py) — with management only "evaluating a return to opportunistic share repurchases later this year" (Q2 2026 call, via search). The forward tailwind is ~0, which is one reason scenario starts were offset below the engine's g_base rather than taken from it. Not double-counted in the verdict.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (fired on the preliminary run at 4.51x): after the growth recalibration the final spread is 2.97x ($71.79 / $24.19).
